subject.title: [security] Nomad provider can forward ACL token across cross-origin redirects

question: Should maintainers treat the public Nomad redirect behavior as an in-scope credential-destination security fix and land a same-origin redirect guard for the Nomad SDK client?
rationale: The source matches the documented credential-destination boundary, but security-sensitive repair and release handling should be explicitly maintainer-owned rather than auto-queued.

options.title: Patch Nomad Redirect Handling
options.body: Land a narrow Nomad adapter fix with redirect regression tests and handle release/security communication as needed.

options.title: Downgrade To Hardening
options.body: Document why redirects from the configured Nomad endpoint are outside the supported boundary and leave code unchanged.

options.title: Defer For Broader Provider Policy
options.body: Pause this item until maintainers decide whether all SDK-backed providers need a shared redirect policy surface.

recommendation.title: Patch Nomad Redirect Handling
recommendation.body: Land a narrow Nomad adapter fix with redirect regression tests and handle release/security communication as needed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the current security-doc boundary and adjacent provider redirect hardening history.
